title: Perimeter Security & Intrusion Detection
metaDescription: Outer-boundary design integrating detection, assessment, and delay, with interim and permanent intrusion detection technology matched to the site.
heroDek: A perimeter that only slows an adversary down, without telling anyone it's happening, isn't doing its job. GSS designs detection, assessment, and delay as one integrated layer, not three separate purchases.
contextHeading: The perimeter has one job. Buy time to know and to act.
contextParagraphs: Perimeter security has three functions that only work as a set. Detection tells the site something is happening, assessment confirms what it is, and delay buys the time needed to respond to it. A perimeter that delays without detecting, or detects without assessment, fails the protective strategy regardless of how well any single piece performs on its own.

GSS evaluates and designs both interim (rapidly deployable) and permanent intrusion detection technology, matched to the site's terrain, its nuisance-alarm environment, and the detection requirement the Design Basis Threat actually demands. Selection is driven by that requirement, not by whichever technology is easiest to install.
Detection timing is coordinated directly with pathway and timeline analysis, so the perimeter's contribution to the timeline is validated by measurement rather than assumed from a datasheet.

methodology.label: Boundary & Terrain Assessment
methodology.body: Perimeter geometry, terrain, and nuisance-alarm sources catalogued.

methodology.label: Detection Requirement Definition
methodology.body: Probability-of-detection and nuisance-alarm-rate requirements set against the protective strategy.

methodology.label: Technology Selection
methodology.body: Sensor, video assessment, and lighting technology selected and matched to terrain and requirement, interim or permanent.

methodology.label: Delay Integration
methodology.body: Perimeter delay elements, such as fencing and barriers, coordinated with detection placement rather than specified separately.

methodology.label: Commissioning & Tuning
methodology.body: System commissioned and nuisance-alarm rate tuned against live site conditions.

methodology.label: Performance Validation
methodology.body: Detection performance validated against the timeline requirement it was designed to meet.

faq.q: What's the difference between interim and permanent IDS?
faq.a: Interim systems are rapidly deployable for temporary or urgent-need coverage; permanent systems are engineered, commissioned installations for the long term. Sites often need both at different points.

faq.q: How do you keep nuisance alarms from wearing out a response force?
faq.a: Through sensor selection matched to the specific terrain and environment, then tuning against live site conditions after commissioning, not a generic default configuration.

faq.q: Does GSS design the perimeter, or only evaluate what's already installed?
faq.a: Both. New perimeter design for facilities that need it, and independent evaluation of existing systems for sites assessing what they already have.
